title: Stitchwork Lunchbox Lumps
tagline: A mad doctor's packed lunch, sewn together and sulking in a sock.
servings: Serves 1 brave soul and a very patient ghoul
rhyme:
Stitch a lunch and stir it right,
Cyclops eyeball, wobbly, bright!
Troll toenails clatter, crunchy and yellow,
Goblin bogeys, green and mellow.
A witch's old sock, darned at the heel,
Lends the lot a whiff of last week's meal.
Cobweb floss in a sticky grey fluff,
Swamp sludge splat, and that's enough!
Dragon scales jingle, clink and chime,
Pantomime bolt, and lunch is on time!

ingredients.item: witch's old sock, darned at the heel

steps: Sew the sock to the cauldron's rim with moonbeam thread, then tip in the sludge till it gurgles and burps in its bed.
Slide in the eyeball and let it look round, then add the troll toenails with a crunchy great pound.
Ladle the bogeys, three glossy green spoons, and stir widdershins thirteen times to a creepy old tune.
Drape on the cobwebs, all sticky and grey, then scatter the scales and they'll jingle away.
Plant the cardboard bolt high with a theatrical cheer, then pack it all up and holler, 'Lunch is here!'
image_prompt: A battered tin lunchbox open on a stone laboratory bench, filled with a lumpy grey-green stew. A glossy jellied eyeball stares upward, yellow toenail crescents poke out, a patched woollen sock droops over the edge, grey cobweb fluff sits on top, shiny scales glint, and a cardboard zigzag bolt stands in the middle.
alt_text: An open tin lunchbox of lumpy green-grey stew topped with a jelly eyeball, toenails, cobweb fluff, a darned sock and a cardboard zigzag bolt.
caption_hook: Mary Shelley gave us a lab, a stitched-up guest and a rather lonely lunch hour. We've packed him a sandwich. Would you swap your lunchbox for this one?
